title: UK fixed-income market recommended closed all day for Easter Monday — with New York trading a full session and Tokyo's USD desk half-closing
source: NEWS: sifma.org/resources/guides-playbooks/holiday-schedule ('Holiday Schedule'), fetched direct 2026-09-05 (HTTP 200, 298,926 bytes) and read out of the page's embedded Next.js flight payload by this session, where the 2027 panels live behind a year tab a rendered-DOM parse never reaches. The U.K. 2027 panel's Easter Monday card reads exactly ['Easter Monday', 'Monday, March 29, 2027'] with NO early-close note attached — the full-closure shape, structurally distinct from the 'Early Close' cards elsewhere on the same page. The causing holiday is independently statutory: gov.uk/bank-holidays.json (HTTP 200, 22,207 bytes) lists '2027-03-29 | Easter Monday' in the england-and-wales division and in northern-ireland, and NOT in scotland. Cross-checked the same day against the page's U.S. panel, whose only March-2027 string is 'Early Close (2:00 p.m. Eastern Time): Thursday, March 25, 2027' and whose 2027 holidays run New Year's Day, MLK 01-18, Presidents 02-15, Good Friday 03-26, Memorial Day 05-31 — no 03-29 entry of any kind, so the recommended US fixed-income tape runs a full session while London is dark. Filed estimate on three counts, identical to the five sifma-* entries already on this calendar: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for an industry trade association's recommended schedule, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and SIFMA's own page states its schedule is a recommendation rather than a market-wide halt each firm is bound by. Unlike its Japan-panel counterpart on the same date, this UK card carries NO 'Tentative' flag.
notes: DISCOVERED during the sifma-japan-early-close-2027-03-29 initial research (2026-09-05). WHY IT EARNS A ROW: it is the CAUSE of the Japan-panel entry already tracked on this date, and it mirrors the accepted sifma-uk-bond-market-closure-2026-12-28 precedent exactly. SCOPE, stated because a sibling entry was originally filed with the wrong reading of it: SIFMA's page says verbatim that 'All SIFMA holiday recommendations apply to the trading of U.S. dollar-denominated government securities...', so every regional panel is a TIME ZONE, not an asset class — this is the London session of the US DOLLAR bond market recommended shut, and UK gilts are out of scope entirely. THE THREE-REGION STATE ON 2027-03-29: UK fully shut (this entry) - Japan 15:00 JST early close, tentative (sifma-japan-early-close-2027-03-29) - US a full session (no card). That is the same inverted triple the 2026-12-28 pair produced, and it instantiates the naming rule this calendar's Japan entries now document: a US holiday shuts Tokyo's dollar desk in full, a UK-only bank holiday halves it. IMPACT LOW: nothing UK-listed is closed by this recommendation (LSE's own equity and gilt hours are not SIFMA's to set, and gov.uk's statutory Easter Monday is what actually shuts London), no house playbook is calendar-, holiday- or rates-keyed (both playbook docs grepped this session for 'holiday|jpx|tokyo|nikkei|closure|jgb|gilt|sifma|easter|fiscal year|ex-dividend': zero hits), and this repo tracks no UK-listed symbol or gilt instrument. HONEST LIMIT: the statutory holiday covers England-and-Wales and Northern Ireland but NOT Scotland, so 'the UK is shut' is true of the venue that matters and not uniformly true; and SIFMA's recommendation is non-binding by its own terms. CORRIDOR CONTEXT: this date already carries boj-summary-of-opinions-2027-03-29 (08:50 JST), ftc-v-amazon-antitrust-trial-2027-03-29 and the Japan early close, and it is the third-to-last Tokyo session of the Japanese fiscal year (FY2026 ends 2027-03-31).
